findings.label: historical-baseline-unavailable
findings.summary: The stated private materialization cannot support stale-anchor checks against shaped_against.
findings.detail: The deterministic layer materializes only the committed HEAD plus package, and self-hosting describes a fresh repository with one commit. Yet stale checks must compare citations against an older shaped_against commit and detect removed identifiers such as cited_bytes. A one-commit materialization cannot do that, so a wrong implementation can pass current fixtures while silently skipping historical validation. Materialize the full required git history (or separately materialize shaped_against) and test both line drift and removed identifiers.

findings.label: controller-config-omitted
findings.summary: The Build changes .kogen/config.yaml even though the running controller reads it, but controller-read auditing deliberately excludes it.
findings.detail: The self-hosting contract says the controller reads .kogen/config.yaml at Build start and freezes role assignment; this Intent adds four auditor entries there. Deterministic controller-read paths are defined as a union that explicitly omits config, so the changed controller input is not guarded or reported. This also conflicts with the Shaper rule against configuration-driven behavior. Either move auditor settings out of config into a compiled/Build-owned setting, or include .kogen/config.yaml in the controller-read/frozen-path contract and prove the pre-edit read semantics.

findings.label: auditor-profile-contract
findings.summary: Selected live fixtures use fast profiles that violate the required route-specific auditor assignment.
findings.detail: The stated route contract requires Claude routes to use Claude Opus 5.5 high and Codex/adversarial-Codex routes to use Codex gpt-6-sol high. The paid-target risk instead says both fixtures configure luna-low/sonnet-low and therefore do not exercise the required auditor profile. The live claims must either run the mandated profiles (with a budget-compatible fixture) or explicitly stop claiming live proof of the auditor layer and add a separate proof for the exact assignment.

findings.label: unproven-case-budget
findings.summary: The package admits 600-second live cases remain unproven while treating the assumption as settled/ready.
findings.detail: questions.md records that all live-shaping-quality cases fitting 600 seconds is unproven, with the remaining choice deferred to the Shaper, but ## Left undecided is None and the package's process forbids presenting a Draft ready with any unproven assumption. The Build is expected to settle this only after admission, contradicting the risk-first ready gate. Add a bounded probe covering every selected case before approval, or keep the Draft explicitly not-ready with a real product question.

findings.label: probe-ownership-contradiction
findings.summary: The root/helper ownership contract is contradictory for paid and harness probes.
findings.detail: INTENT.md and front-loaded-questions require the root to delegate every paid and harness probe and remain idle. risks.yaml paid-targets-and-time says paid or harness probes stay with the root. A Developer can satisfy either statement and violate the other, so the caller and execution policy are ambiguous. Remove the stale root-owned clause and retain one exact rule, including who may launch the selected paid target.

findings.label: cut-live-fixture-contract
findings.summary: The truncated scenarios file hides required live-target route, login, preflight, and observation contracts.
findings.detail: scenarios.yaml is marked CUT at 24,000 of 86,446 bytes. The supplied text does not expose the fixture route, role profiles, login binding, readiness preflights, per-case budgets, or the exact observation for either selected paid target. Those are mandatory audit checks, so this package cannot be validated from the bounded artifact. Include the complete live-shaping-quality and live-shape-to-build scenario/fixture definitions (or an untruncated evidence manifest) before approval.
